name: Fibroblast
blurb: The main cell of connective tissue: a long, flat, tapering cell with an oval nucleus and a well-developed protein-making and packaging system. It makes the fibres and gel that fill the space around it.
note: Model: a human fibroblast of connective tissue, drawn as an active (matrix-making) cell and cut in half along its length. Measured: its shape as a long, spindle-like cell with an oval nucleus of about 500 µm³ (human fibroblasts), and a rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus that are prominent when the cell is active. Two or more nucleoli are described in the literature; two are drawn (illustrative). Illustrative: the nucleus placed at the centre of the cell, the number of nucleoli, the length, width and thickness drawn, the nucleus axes (chosen to match the measured volume), the numbers and sizes of mitochondria, lysosomes and Golgi stacks, and all colours. Real fibroblasts are branched and vary with the tissue; this is one simplified, smooth example.

length.note: illustrative. In one thin section of the wall of the small intestine (jejunum; species not stated) a fibroblast measured about 25 µm along its long axis (histguide_em006), but a section cuts the cell short, so this is a lower bound. The range is a guess.

length_in_section.note: estimated from the scale bar of one electron micrograph of a spindle-shaped fibroblast in the wall of the small intestine (jejunum); the species is not stated on the page. A thin slice, so a lower bound on the true length.

width.note: illustrative: wide enough to hold the nucleus drawn (9 µm across)

thickness.note: illustrative: a flattened cell, not a round rod

nucleus_volume.note: a database entry for the volume of a human fibroblast nucleus, taken from a review of nuclear structure; BioNumbers flags the entry as needing a better reference, so treat it as a rough value

nucleus_axes.calc: an ellipsoid 19 x 9 x 5.5 µm has a volume of pi/6 x 19 x 9 x 5.5 = 493 µm³, close to the 500 µm³ measured
nucleus_axes.note: illustrative axes; only their product is tied to the measurement. 'Elongated nucleus' is the shape in the sources (histguide_em006).

cultured_cell_volume.note: mean volume of human diploid fibroblasts that had stopped dividing, grown in dish culture and sized with an electron counter; not a cell in tissue. Given only to show the order of size; the drawn cell is not tuned to it.

size_um.note: illustrative axes giving the measured volume of about 500 µm³ (bionumbers_nuc); the sources call the nucleus oval or elongated, not give its axes

nucleus.nucleoli_note: illustrative: two or more are described in life (wikipedia_fibroblast); the nucleolus is not visible in the micrograph (histguide_em006)
nucleus.position_note: illustrative: placed at the centre of the cell; no source read gives a position

volume_fraction.note: illustrative; no source read gives a volume share for fibroblasts

mitochondria.note: the micrograph description calls them oval or rod-shaped with visible cristae (histguide_em006); their number and size here are illustrative

stacks.note: illustrative number; the sources say only that the Golgi apparatus is prominent in an active fibroblast (histguide_em006)

not_drawn: collagen fibres and the gel outside the cell

special.note: In an active fibroblast the rough endoplasmic reticulum is abundant: flattened sacs studded with ribosomes, in which proteins for export are made and first modified. It is the most striking feature of the cell in an electron micrograph. Not drawn: the picture shows the Golgi apparatus that follows the rough endoplasmic reticulum but not the reticulum itself, so it should not be read as a cell without it.

Proteins made on the rough endoplasmic reticulum pass to the Golgi apparatus, are modified and sorted there, and leave in secretory vesicles that fuse with the cell surface. Fibroblasts export the protein and sugar parts of the fibres and gel of connective tissue this way. The vesicles and the matrix they feed are not drawn.
A fibroblast is described as having a branched cytoplasm and more projections than its parent mesenchymal cell. The cell here is drawn smooth with two tapering tips; the branches are not drawn.

Two places reach this cell: loose connective tissue between organs and around fat cells, and the outer fibrous layer of the perichondrium around cartilage, which holds type I collagen, fibroblasts and blood vessels. The cell is the same kind in both; how long and how flat it is in each place is not measured here.

cut: The cell is cut in half along its length, through the middle of the flattened body: the long oval nucleus with two nucleoli lies in the thick middle, with Golgi stacks beside it, rod-shaped mitochondria and small lysosomes scattered through the cytoplasm, and the body tapering to a point at each end.

colours.convention: Cell membrane pale and the inside dark; nucleus violet; mitochondria orange; the other organelles in code colours. None of these colours is real: in life the cell is nearly colourless.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.about: The watery inside of the cell, crowded with proteins. In an active fibroblast much of it is taken up by the protein-making and packaging system.

about: A fibroblast lies among the fibres of connective tissue: in the loose tissue that packs spaces between organs and around fat cells, and in the outer layer of the perichondrium, the skin around cartilage, where it is described as lying among type I collagen with blood vessels. It is the most abundant cell of connective tissue, and it makes the fibres and the gel between them.

The cell is drawn about 80 µm long, 14 µm wide and 7 µm thick, with a volume of {drawn.cellVolume} µm³. These sizes are illustrative: the only measured length quoted here, about 25 µm, comes from one thin slice that cuts the cell short. Only the nucleus is tied to a measurement, a volume of about 500 µm³ in human fibroblasts (a BioNumbers entry that its own compilers flag as needing a better reference), drawn here as a long oval {drawn.nuclei} nucleus with two nucleoli (the number is illustrative).

This is drawn as an active cell. A resting one, sometimes called a fibrocyte, is smaller and has less rough endoplasmic reticulum. Not drawn: the rough endoplasmic reticulum itself, the cell's thin branches, the fibres and the filaments inside the cell that pull on them. No neighbouring cells or junctions are drawn.
